standard.name: MIxS (Minimum Information about any (x) Sequence)
standard.abstract: MIxS describes contextual metadata for sequenced samples (genomes, metagenomes, marker genes, MAGs, single-cell genomes). It is used across environmental, host-associated, and laboratory-derived sampling scenarios and records metadata about sampling environment, sample handling, nucleic acid extraction and library/sequencing methods. The recorded data are metadata fields (strings, numbers, controlled vocabularies, and structured patterns) that accompany sequence data submissions.

classification.rationale: MIxS "is a standard from the Genomic Standards Consortium (GSC) for reporting contextual metadata about sequenced samples. It defines checklists for genomic sequence types (for example genomes, metagenomes, and marker genes), environmental extensions, and the terms that populate them." (source: mixs index)

samp_name.name: sample name
samp_name.descr: A local identifier or name that for the material sample used for extracting nucleic acids, and subsequent sequencing. It can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples.
samp_name.evidence: "A local identifier or name that for the material sample used for extracting nucleic acids, and subsequent sequencing. It can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab, and as informative as possible. INSDC requires every sample name from a single Submitter to be unique. Use of a globally unique identifier for the field source_mat_id is recommended in addition to sample_name" (Term: sample name, mixs)

alt.name: altitude
alt.descr: Heights of objects such as airplanes, space shuttles, rockets, atmospheric balloons and heights of places such as atmospheric layers and clouds. It is used to measure the height of an object which is above the earth's surface. In this context, the altitude measurement is the vertical distance between the earth's surface above sea level and the sampled position in the air
alt.evidence: "Altitude is a term used to identify heights of objects such as airplanes, space shuttles, rockets, atmospheric balloons and heights of places such as atmospheric layers and clouds. It is used to measure the height of an object which is above the earth's surface. In this context, the altitude measurement is the vertical distance between the earth's surface above sea level and the sampled position in the air" (Term: altitude, mixs)
